script.base: The book has Buffalo laying 3 with a 55 total, so the base script is a competitive shootout, not a slog and not a blowout: BUF implied 29, BAL implied 26. Both lead backs stay involved early — James Cook 59 carries for 281 yards in weeks 4-6, Derrick Henry 58 carries for 205 in weeks 5-7 — but 55 points means both passing games stay live. Khalil Shakir (17 targets, 196 yards, only 73 air yards) is the Bills chain-mover into Baltimore's middle, and Zay Flowers (31 targets, 256 yards, 211 air yards) is the Ravens alpha, with Josh Cuevas (10 targets, 105 yards) already in the rotation. Wind 8.0 and 69.4F do not take away downfield or short throws.
script.flip1: Buffalo jumps ahead by two scores. Cook's 19.7-carry pace and Josh Allen's 17 carries / 129 rush yards from weeks 4-6 salt the clock, Shakir and Keon Coleman late targets stall, and Baltimore abandons Henry (3.53 YPC) so Flowers, Rashod Bateman, Mark Andrews and Cuevas targets spike. That flip helps Ravens receiving overs and hurts a Bills WR over.
script.flip2: Baltimore leads and grinds. Henry's carry count expands and a 10-plus run — Buffalo has allowed 18 such runs in 6 games, and Henry already has a 102-rush / 120 rush-plus-rec week in the last4 — clears a high rush number. Buffalo then throws more, which helps Shakir, Coleman (228 air yards) and Dalton Kincaid, and can cut Henry's efficiency if the game stays a track meet instead of a grind.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both lost. Shakir: Buffalo led by two scores after halftime, Cook's 20-carry pace and Allen's 129 rush yards of scramble/designed runs from the weeks 4-6 window killed the clock, and Shakir posted another 6-yard game like the one already in his last4; or the Baltimore middle number (only 51 attempts) was noise and they took away the hook, pushing air yards to Coleman, whose last4 already includes a 7. The missing week-7 Bills offense log is the other hole — if that game already showed the target share moving to Coleman (15 targets, 228 air yards) or Palmer (last4 34, 43, 3, 37), this over was stale before kickoff. Cuevas: the consensus was right. A fifth option behind Flowers (31 targets), Andrews (13), Bateman (11) and Hill (11) got scripted out in a one-score game, the 14/26/44/35 yards were garbage-time we could not split without play-by-play, and he finished under 9.5 while the no-vig over sat at 0.492 the whole time. A late inactive not on the morning report would also zero him. Those counter-cases are real, which is why both legs are flagged for the human; they are not stronger than four games of a 14-yard Cuevas floor plus Shakir's primary-target overlap with a 9.04 middle, so they are not dropped.
slip_story: One shootout story for a 55 total and a 3-point spread: both offenses throw, Buffalo's slot finds the Baltimore middle, and Baltimore's short-area rotation still eats in a 26-point implied day. Shakir recyds over 41.5 and Cuevas recyds over 9.5 win together if the game stays competitive and pass-heavy. They split if Buffalo blows out and runs (hurts Shakir, can help Cuevas as Baltimore throws) or if Baltimore grinds with Henry (hurts Cuevas's target share, can still leave Shakir live). Each leg survives the base and one flip and is tagged script-dependent on the other flip. Do not add a game-total under, a Henry under, a Cook over into a 3.82 YPC defense, a TD, or a second market on either player. Two-leg slip only. No bet is placed.
